rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant prismatic/cantilevered mass, so gesture clarity is moderate, but the four-view set also shows a somewhat abrupt, top-heavy section with limited public void articulation. The blue access edge is not answered by a convincing entry seam, court, or undercut; the ground response feels largely sealed or incidental. The silhouette is coherent but leans toward an arbitrary stepped/stacked object rather than a clearly capacity-bearing section. It does not fail because of fragmentation or view inconsistency, but it also does not yet support the neighborhood-living brief strongly enough: there is not enough active ground threshold, public courtyard logic, or sectionally legible mixed-use hierarchy. Reference 1 and 2 suggest a more explicit porous base and courtyard publicness; reference 4 supports a stronger podium/upper-mass split, while reference 5 is useful only as a counterfactual to borrow permeability/bridge intent without copying its typology.
